definitions.gloss: disaster preparedness supplies; emergency supplies; disaster kit
definitions.explanation: Items kept on hand in preparation for natural disasters such as earthquakes, typhoons, and floods. Includes food, water, flashlights, first-aid kits, batteries, and other survival essentials. A culturally important concept in disaster-prone Japan.

examples.japanese: {防災|ぼうさい}グッズを{準備|じゅんび}しておこう。
{防災|ぼうさい}グッズはどこに{売|う}っていますか。
examples.english: Where can I buy disaster preparedness supplies?

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{後|あと}、{防災|ぼうさい}グッズを{見直|みなお}す{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: After the earthquake, more people reviewed their disaster supplies.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}{全員分|ぜんいんぶん}の{防災|ぼうさい}グッズを{一|ひと}つのリュックにまとめてある。
examples.english: I've packed disaster supplies for the whole family into one backpack.

notes:
Composed of {防災|ぼうさい} (disaster prevention/preparedness) and グッズ (goods, items — from English). This is the standard everyday term for the emergency supplies that many Japanese households keep ready.

Japan's frequent earthquakes, typhoons, and other natural disasters make {防災|ぼうさい}グッズ a familiar concept in daily life. Home centers, convenience stores, and online shops sell pre-assembled kits, and September 1 ({防災|ぼうさい}の{日|ひ}, Disaster Prevention Day) is a common time for people to check and refresh their supplies.

Typical items include {非常食|ひじょうしょく} (emergency food), {懐中電灯|かいちゅうでんとう} (flashlight), {携帯|けいたい}ラジオ (portable radio), {飲料水|いんりょうすい} (drinking water), and {救急|きゅうきゅう}セット (first-aid kit).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {防災|ぼうさい}グッズを{準備|じゅんび}する: to prepare emergency supplies
- {防災|ぼうさい}グッズを{見直|みなお}す: to review/update one's disaster supplies
- {防災|ぼうさい}グッズを{揃|そろ}える: to assemble disaster supplies
- {防災|ぼうさい}グッズ{一式|いっしき}: a full set of emergency supplies

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {非常持|ひじょうも}ち{出|だ}し{袋|ぶくろ}: emergency go-bag — the bag itself for evacuating with essential supplies
- {備蓄品|びちくひん}: stockpiled supplies — a more formal term for stored provisions
- {防災|ぼうさい}セット: disaster preparedness set — a near-synonym, emphasizing a pre-packaged kit
